item.title: What Really Happens When Linux Deletes a File?
item.description:
What Really Happens When Linux Deletes a File?

When we type:

rm test.txt

Most people think:

Linux deletes the file immediately.

But this is not exactly true.

Linux does not directly erase data.

The real question:

What does deleting a file actually mean?

1. What Happens When We Execute rm?

First:

rm test.txt

is not a kernel operation.

rm is a user-space program.

Check:

Example:

item.title: How Does Linux Find the Real Socket From an Integer FD?
item.description:
How Does Linux Find the Real Socket From an Integer FD?

In the previous article, we learned:

int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);

returns an integer.

But this creates another question:

If a socket is represented only by an integer, how does Linux find the real socket object inside the kernel?

For example:

read(fd, buffer, size);

The application only provides:

But inside the kernel, Linux needs to locate:
